about: Wording that is never wanted. The CLI refuses it in script.md, and in the explainer's points and captions where 'in' says so (one repair turn naming each sentence), and the hub refuses an upload that still has it (SPEC.md section 6). Only what is never wanted belongs here; what is sometimes right (a caveat, a comparison, a strong word) is left to the cut-only pass, not to a list. To grow a class, add a phrase. A phrase matches as whole words, ignoring case unless case_sensitive; ' matches both apostrophes; a trailing * is any word ending; ... is a gap of up to two words. The class listener_name refuses the listener's own name: the name of the person the episode is made for (the uploader) is added to its phrases at check time, so its list here may be empty.

classes.fix: Delete the name: the text is about the paper and is addressed to no one.

classes.wrong: narrates what the listener knows, has done or keeps in notes
classes.fix: Delete that part. A concept the listener knows is used by name with no explanation and no word about who knows it; a concept the listener does not know is explained without saying so.

classes.wrong: talks about the episode or the narrator's plan
classes.fix: Delete it and let the content itself come next; for "today" say "current" or "now".
Delete it: no venue, review status, anonymity or preprint status. Say what the paper does.
Delete the phrase, or say the thing in the plain words a colleague would use at a whiteboard.

classes.wrong: announces the idea or the conclusion instead of stating it
classes.fix: Delete the announcement and state the idea itself as a claim about the method.
phrases: one idea to hold on to
what the paper shows, in the end
in the end, what the paper shows
